t: They leave their boots in the doorway, and I trip over them every night.
We need another blanket before the cold settles in.
They fixed the loose peg after I complained once. I should notice that aloud.
The house is small enough that every disagreement fills it.
I like hearing them move around while I am half asleep.
We should invite somebody for supper before we forget how.
They always leave the warmer side of the hearth for me.
I promised to patch the draft three days ago.
We finally agree where the table belongs. It only took a season.
Their cup is beside mine every morning. I still like seeing that.
I should bring something home besides work on my clothes.
They talk in their sleep and deny every word by daylight.
The floor needs sweeping, but sitting together sounds better tonight.
We have two opinions about every repair and one set of tools.
They know when I am worried before I say anything.
I was angry this morning. I should go home kinder than I left.
The rain sounds better when somebody else is listening beside you.
We keep saving the good bowl for each other.
I should tell them I will be late before late becomes worry.
The house is ours, including the leaks and the arguments.
The latch sticks when the air is damp.
I should move the stool before I bruise my leg on it again.
The roof held through last night. I checked twice anyway.
A little ash keeps finding its way onto every clean surface.
I need a proper place for wet clothes.
The door shuts cleanly now. That repair was worth the trouble.
I can find the water cup in complete darkness.
The chimney draws poorly when the wind comes from the east.
I should hang herbs near the window. The room smells too much like smoke.
There is always one more small repair once I start looking.
My coat has a peg, my cup has a shelf, and I have a bed.
I heard rain and stayed where I was. That still feels luxurious.
The floor is cold, but at least there is a floor.
I should bank the fire before leaving tomorrow.
This place looks better after five minutes of putting things away.
I want to believe the good days mean something. Wanting is not proof.
I have prayed twice this week and felt foolish only once.
Some people sound certain because they never ask themselves difficult questions.
{god} feels close today. Yesterday, there was only weather.
I keep noticing answers after deciding nobody listened.
Belief would be easier if everyone stopped explaining it to me.
I trust what I saw. I do not trust what people say it meant.
Maybe gratitude is enough without certainty.
I nearly thanked {god} this morning. Nearly still counts for something.
Every miracle gives me one answer and three new questions.
I envy people whose faith stays the same all day.
Silence feels like absence until something unexpected happens.
I am not faithless. I am simply unconvinced before breakfast.
The village believes loudly. My belief speaks under its breath.
I would like one quiet sign that nobody else interprets for me.
